A second device can remain open after account-wide membership cleanup; if still OPEN its next PING triggers the unchanged credential recheck and closure, rather than assuming membership removal always immediately closes every socket.

evidence.scenarioScope: Unauthorized edits produce no data changes or events.
evidence.rationale: Reviewed source assertions matched to this exact file/title in the recorded execution; scope and omissions remain explicit.

SQLite retains all three original unredacted rows; separate recreated Miniflare runtime independently reads both histories with unrelated content preserved.

evidence.testTitle: sqlite 10485760 byte real upload limits MEDIA-009 MEDIA-012 ABUSE-007: oversized and exhausted quota denials are silent and inert across restart
evidence.scenarioScope: SQLite upload size and full 100 MiB quota with actual 10 MiB objects, observed denial windows and restart.
evidence.rationale: Reviewed source assertions matched to this exact file/title in the recorded execution; scope and omissions remain explicit.
assertionDetails: Independent Alice, Bob and Charlie authenticate via public registration, login and IRC PASS; Alice and Bob join a secret channel and Charlie is outside it. SQLite stores real upload bytes in workerd persistence.

Both upload aliases reject actual 10 MiB+1 request bodies with 413 and no Location, content or UUID; filling exactly 100 MiB with 10 MiB objects succeeds, and both aliases reject further payloads with 403 without Location, payload or UUID.

Before and after each rejection, three live IRC clients and three ticket event streams receive shared-channel barriers; no additional IRC or event data is delivered in the rejection window. A test-only read-only SQLite metadata accessor and, for R2, actual bucket object listing remain identical across each denial.

Bob downloads a channel-scoped positive object with the expected SHA256 while Charlie gets 404; Bob’s independent private object remains readable. Owner deletion frees quota and permits replacement, whose bytes are checked after an independent workerd restart.

Stopped workerd SQLite metadata matches the pre-stop state, including owner, scope, sizes, storage kind and SQLite bytes length; R2 object listing remains identical after restart. A restored six-stream observer window confirms another legacy-alias quota denial is silent and inert.
SQLite stores bounded chunks with metadata and digest in one transaction; retained payload is downloaded and compared byte-for-byte via SHA256 after restart. R2 uses the real Miniflare bucket.

evidence.testTitle: idle kick takes effect on reconstructed recipients with scoped delivery and persistent state
evidence.scenarioScope: Owner KICK removes Bob from #vault; Bob’s still-live barrier IRC and event recipients receive no later #vault payload, history/read and write are denied, and stopped SQLite has no Bob vault membership. After restart Bob may rejoin and receives restored traffic.
evidence.rationale: Reviewed source assertions matched to this exact file/title in the recorded execution; scope and omissions remain explicit.
assertionDetails: Real independent rootadmin, Alice, Bob and Charlie register and authenticate through REST and IRC PASS; Alice/Bob share secret #vault, Charlie owns independent secret #unrelated, and all three share #barrier with real ticket-authenticated event streams.

A real protected message and event reach Bob before local workerd central SessionDO and observed event-edge shard eviction; afterward a separate shared-channel marker reaches Bob’s still-idle IRC and event sockets before another actor changes authorization.
A forbidden Charlie channel-info mutation returns 403 and leaves the independently read channel info unchanged; live IRC and event observers receive only the explicit shared-channel barrier.

A second local hibernating eviction of the central SessionDO and observed event-edge shards occurs after the transition; Alice posts a fresh protected message unconditionally, receives its event, and the unrelated Charlie socket and stream remain live via a separate marker without receiving the private message.

Post-transition denied operations are followed by another barrier and produce no extra event or IRC payload, except Bob’s expected role-denial numeric; stopped SQLite confirms the authorized message and independent Charlie channel and Alice/Charlie DM remain, and rejected content is absent.

A fresh runtime checks independent Charlie channel and DM reads and the specified persisted revocation, then legitimate reauthorization or credential recovery restores Bob’s IRC and event delivery. These are local workerd hibernation/recreation checks, not deployed Cloudflare observations.

Owner KICK removes Bob from #vault; Bob’s still-live barrier IRC and event recipients receive no later #vault payload, history/read and write are denied, and stopped SQLite has no Bob vault membership. After restart Bob may rejoin and receives restored traffic.

The v2 event stream tracks a ticket-derived shard and the test hibernates every observed event edge shard as well as the central SessionDO; it does not assert that all three streams occupy distinct shards.

reviewProvenance.reason: Hibernation now covers the central SessionDO and actual ticket-selected event edge shards, not a single all-in-one SessionDO.

evidence.testTitle: WS-021 ABUSE-012: a real paused event TCP reader resumes private frames within negotiated credit while independent recipients progress without proving a provider buffer ceiling
evidence.scenarioScope: A live v2 event reader is paused below negotiated credit and resumed before the reader challenge deadline while independent authorized and outsider recipients are observed.
evidence.rationale: Reviewed source assertions matched to this exact file/title in the recorded execution; scope and omissions remain explicit.
assertionDetails: After a live positive marker, the real WebSocket/TCP reader is paused and 12 private REST messages are published with matching saved IDs and content; an independent authorized IRC/event recipient progresses while outsider Dave sees no private bodies.

During the bounded pause the socket remains open and local domain frame/byte counters do not advance; request content is less than half the negotiated byte limit and elapsed time is less than the challenge timeout.

On resume, the private message IDs match all 12 saved IDs exactly in order, received wire bytes remain below negotiated credit, at least one challenge was observed and acknowledged by the helper, and the socket stays open. This finite credit scenario does not establish provider memory allocation or the separate non-acknowledging hard-close path.
Forbidden outsider history remains 403 with live barriers; stored message IDs/content, unrelated content and fresh authorized delivery survive runtime recreation.

evidence.scenarioScope: Account reenable after actual disable, with independent role and channel controls.
evidence.rationale: Reviewed source assertions matched to this exact file/title in the recorded execution; scope and omissions remain explicit.
assertionDetails: Real founder, active IRC operator, ordinary, revoked and anonymous actors cannot grant/revoke Bob admin or enable a disabled account on either alias; four IRC and event observers have a message barrier around denials.
Administrator grants and revokes Bob oper via both aliases; Bob uses OPER on the already connected socket, then revocation emits -o and the same socket is denied OPER and SAJOIN.

Before and after each denial block, independent read-only SQLite snapshots compare normalized users, role and nickname rows, user metadata and credential digests plus the founder-channel configuration and grants; session rows and account timestamps are excluded.

evidence.testTitle: WS-021 ABUSE-012: a real paused event TCP reader resumes private frames within negotiated credit while independent recipients progress without proving a provider buffer ceiling
evidence.scenarioScope: A live v2 event reader is paused below negotiated credit and resumed before the reader challenge deadline while independent authorized and outsider recipients are observed.
evidence.rationale: Reviewed source assertions matched to this exact file/title in the recorded execution; scope and omissions remain explicit.
assertionDetails: After a live positive marker, the real WebSocket/TCP reader is paused and 12 private REST messages are published with matching saved IDs and content; an independent authorized IRC/event recipient progresses while outsider Dave sees no private bodies.

During the bounded pause the socket remains open and local domain frame/byte counters do not advance; request content is less than half the negotiated byte limit and elapsed time is less than the challenge timeout.

On resume, the private message IDs match all 12 saved IDs exactly in order, received wire bytes remain below negotiated credit, at least one challenge was observed and acknowledged by the helper, and the socket stays open. This finite credit scenario does not establish provider memory allocation or the separate non-acknowledging hard-close path.
Forbidden outsider history remains 403 with live barriers; stored message IDs/content, unrelated content and fresh authorized delivery survive runtime recreation.
transports: real SQLite/provider observations as explicitly stated

evidence.testTitle: ABUSE-013: persistent real account RPC failure keeps ordered channel work bounded with paced alarms and recovers after authority returns
evidence.scenarioScope: Finite, fixed-workload persistent account-authority RPC failure with real scheduled alarms, privacy controls, ordered recovery and local recreation.
evidence.rationale: Reviewed source assertions matched to this exact file/title in the recorded execution; scope and omissions remain explicit.
assertionDetails: A real Bob account lookup persistently fails inside Worker SQLite; Bob closes 1008 for authorization failure and his membership is removed. An outsider private history read is 403; Bob’s dependency-failure response is 500 with no queued private content, missing-table name, SQLITE marker or stack field.

One blocked membership intent and two committed messages produce exactly five ordered pending rows. Each of four real scheduled alarm observations compares the complete pending rows, their serialized byte length and next sequence to the original; the source compares bytes dynamically, rather than asserting the diagnostic run’s observed 4,149 bytes as a constant.

At least four genuine alarms span at least three one-second intervals. Each alarm contains exactly one actual recorded failure; the next alarm is no earlier than one second after that failure, and the number of alarms respects the bound derived from the observed time window.

A separate public channel continues delivering actual Charlie-to-Dave IRC and v2 event controls throughout the outage; no same-channel delivery progress is claimed while the ordered private head is blocked.

After fault removal, an existing scheduled alarm drains the original outbox; Alice receives both queued private messages exactly once and in order over IRC and v2 events. Outsider IRC/event observers and Bob’s closed IRC socket omit private content, Bob and outsider private reads are 403 after repair, and stopped SQLite excludes original outbox rows while retaining one row per committed message.

After local runtime recreation the saved messages remain and fresh Alice/Bob authorized delivery works; newly committed shutdown leave intents are distinguished from the recovered original outbox rows.
transports: local Worker SQLite and Durable Object alarms
